INTRODUCTIONM
When dealing with motion, distance is used only to calculate velocity, acceleration, and deceleration.
In motion the main concerns are velocity, acceleration, and deceleration.
When dealing with position the main concern is the starting and ending point of an object.

Position electronics consists of two general areas.........
Generator devices cause a change in position. They are called position or motion generators.
Analog generators include DC, AC servo motors, synchros and transmitting devices.
These devices rotate from one point to another according to an analog input signal.
Digital position generators are stepper motors.............
Steppers rotate from one point to another according to a digital input signal.
Position generators are motors and their characteristics are similar to motion generators.
Sensors are devices that detect a change in position. Position sensors indicate the position of an object.
Analog position sensors are resolvers, synchros, and variable transducers.
Sensors receive a mechanical input from a position generator and produce an analog output. This output represents the position.
Digital position sensors are encoders......................
Encoders are rotated by position generators. Their output is a digital signal that represents position.
Position generators and position sensors are opposite......
Position generators use an electrical signal for the input and produce a mechanical output.
Position sensors use a mechanical input to produce an electrical output.
Position generators and sensors normally use feedback......
FEEDBACK - Feedback is the control of the system. Not all systems contain feedback. Systems containing feedback are called Closed Loop Systems.
DEFINITION
Feedback ensures a specified position is maintained.

A prime mover is a position generator......................
DISCUSSION
Nearly all prime movers produce an output that has circular motion.
The motion is changed to different velocities or to linear motion depending on the type of position change needed.
It is important to be able to calculate the output power of a prime mover.
Power of a prime mover (motor) is equal to the force that turns the shaft times the distance the shaft moves.
It's like electrical power, the force that moves electrons (voltage), times the movement of electrons (current), equals the amount of power (watts).
In motors, the force that turns the shaft or twisting action is measured in Ft
Distance is the change in position per unit of time, which is calculated from RPM or revolutions per minute.

HORSEPOWER - Horse power equals the RPM times the torque divided by 5252.5.
Horsepower is important because most prime movers do not position an object directly.
The driven shaft is used to move the prime mover.
This allows different applications of the prime mover using one type of driven shaft.
The torque, speed, or direction can be changed by using a different prime mover radius.
In all cases, the driven shafts HP (power in) must equal the prime mover HP (power out).
Knowing that power in equals power out, the torque and RPM of the prime mover can be calculated by only knowing the characteristics of the driven shaft.
The formulas for the output torque and RPM are found by using the ratio of the radius times the input values.
These formulas work because power in equals power out.
